confidence_note: Robbins tells the story of Theodore Johnson, an early UPS employee who never earned more than about $14,000 a year but saved 20 percent of every paycheck and bonus, largely in company stock, and was worth around $70 million by the time he was 90. The story is widely reported and appears in the book; the figures are kept as Robbins gives them, rounded. The reference TR text says it opens the book; its exact position is not confirmed and is not claimed. Robbins's broader point is that compounding, not income, builds wealth; he also stresses that Johnson's result depended heavily on UPS stock performing extremely well.
facts: Theodore Johnson worked for UPS from its early years. Robbins says he never made more than about $14,000 a year.
Johnson had one rigid rule: he set aside 20 percent of every paycheck and every bonus he received, largely in company stock.
By the time he was 90, his savings had grown to around $70 million.
He gave much of the money away, including large donations for education.
Robbins uses the story to show the power of compounding: returns earning further returns over long periods.
His point: it's not how much you earn that makes you wealthy, but how much you consistently save and invest, and for how long.
tension: A man who never earned a big salary ended his life with a fortune most executives never reach.
opening_idea: A delivery-company employee with a modest salary dies a multimillionaire, and it wasn't luck at the lottery.

lessons.idea: Savings rate and time matter more than income.
lessons.anchor: 20 percent of every paycheck on a modest salary

lessons.idea: A rigid rule beats good intentions.

reflect: What percentage of your income do you save automatically?
What would a fixed rule change in your finances?
reflect_final: What percentage could you commit to saving from your very next paycheck?

use_cases.situation: You feel you can't build wealth on your current salary.
use_cases.move: Set a fixed percentage that leaves your account automatically every payday.

use_cases.situation: Your young adult child just got their first job.
use_cases.move: Share the Johnson story and help them set up an automatic savings rule.

use_cases.situation: A friend says investing is only for the rich.
use_cases.move: Explain that consistency and time drive compounding more than the amount.

pocket_idea: Wealth grows from what you keep and how long you let it grow.
